messages:
julia: Heads-up — spotted a cluster churn event in us-west1 this morning. Several GPU spot nodes got termination notices but the drain/cordon step only completed for some pods. Autoscaler reacted by provisioning replacements, then they got preempted again. Anyone seen this pattern before?

spot-terminator-bot: Instance gce-spot-gpu-07 received PREEMPTION_NOTICE at 2025-10-14T09:17:12Z (90s warning)

kevin: Uh — did the termination-handler daemonset run on those nodes? If the handler can't exec into kubelet it won't cordon fast. Any errors in node-prober logs?

julia: Logs show handler started but failed to acquire the drain lock for ~60s, then timed out. Some pods had tolerations that prevented eviction (stateful training pods with NoExecute taint toleration).

sara: This is the mixed-capacity pool gotcha: we run a dedicated non-spot pool + a spot mixed instance group with taints. If pods are mis-labeled or use broad tolerations they survive the taint and block drain, autoscaler thinks node is underutilized and spins up more. Suggested fixes: 1) tighten tolerations for long-running workloads 2) run termination-handler as non-privileged but with proper RBAC to cordon/drain 3) prefer draining logic that force-evicts best-effort jobs.

mike: To add: use the spot instance termination handler (we already have a fork). Make it cordon + drain quickly and fall back to `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30 --force` for low-priority training pods. Example snippet we use in canary:

```
# handler action on preemption
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

kevin: Also consider using a taint like `spot=true:PreferNoSchedule` and then only grant NoExecute tolerations to critical infra. That way training jobs will be scheduled on spot but be evictable. Lower the cluster-autoscaler `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to avoid premature downscales during noisy preemptions.

julia: Good call. We should also make training jobs use a lower `priorityClass` + toleration so they get evicted first. For GPU checkpoints: encourage checkpointing every N minutes so we don't lose more than a few steps.

sara: For autoscaler config, switch expander to `least-waste` and set node-group priorities: prefer non-spot for pods with long lived PDBs. Also add `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` for mixed MIGs to avoid weird prefers.

mike: Proposed rollout plan:
- enable termination-handler daemonset in canary k8s-zone (us-west1-b)
- add a `spot-preempt` taint + update training job templates to tolerate `PreferNoSchedule` only
- update CA flags in staging then prod if stable
- run chaos test that injects preemption notices (simulate GCE metadata hook) nightly

julia: Can we add a fast metric in Console: "spot drain success rate" + avg drain latency? If drain > 30s it's costing us extra nodes. :thinking:

kevin: I'll implement the metric and the simulated preempt job this afternoon. I'll also open a small PR to make the handler fallback to `--grace-period=30` for pods with `priorityClass=low`.

sara: Remember PDBs block eviction — set `minAvailable: 0` for best-effort batch jobs or avoid PDBs there. Also update runbooks.

mike: Quick command to deploy the handler canary: `kubectl apply -f infra/spot-termination-handler-canary.yaml -n kube-system`

julia: Thanks all — cheers. Let's monitor for 48h and then roll the config out across other regions if stable. :thumbsup:
